sentences.text:
1. Petitioner is accused in criminal case registered vide Crime No.178/2024 at Police Station Joura,
District Morena for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 376 (2) (n) of IPC has preferred the present petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashment of FIR and consequential proceedings on the sole ground of compromise.

2. Short facts of the case are that upon complaint of respondent No.2/prosecutrix Police Station Joura, District Morena registered the offence against the petitioner wherein it is alleged that the petitioner has committed rape on the pretext of marriage and later on refused to marry.
The petitioner and respondent No.2 entered into wedlock and they are living together.
They have expressed their desire to compound the offence and settled the matter once and for all.

The application is made on behalf of respondent No.2/prosecutrix wherein she confirmed the factum of Jogendra Kushwah vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182293872/
1 compromise and wedlock and she prayed for quashment of the FIR and consequential criminal proceedings on the ground of compromise.
3.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court by order dated 01.05.2024 directed the parties to appear before Principal Registrar of this Court on 08.05.2024 for the purpose of verification of the factum of compromise.

The Principal Registrar has submitted his report dated 08.05.2024 whereby the Principal Registrar has verified the factum of compromise after recording the statement of petitioner/accused and respondent No.2/complainant/prosecutrix who were identified by their respective counsel before the Principal Registrar.

After verifying their identity and after recording their statements, Principal Registrar is of the view that prosecutrix has arrived at compromise with petitioner/accused voluntarily, without any threat, inducement or coercion.
The petitioner has also filed the documents and photographs along with the petition to bolster the submission of solemnization of marriage with prosecutrix after registration of FIR.
4. The core question involved in the present case is whether an offence registered under Section 376 of IPC can be quashed on the basis of the compromise ?

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that prosecutrix was major at the time of commission of alleged offence and she entered into the relationship with the petitioner/accused voluntarily with her free consent.

However, the report was lodged only due to failure on the part of the petitioner to solemnize marriage with the prosecutrix and as after registration of FIR both of them have already solemnized the marriage, therefore, the FIR be quashed.

6. Shri Vijay Kumar Jha, Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No.2/prosecutrix submits that prosecutrix has voluntarily entered into compromise with the petitioner and both of them have solemnized the marriage, therefore, FIR be quashed.

7. After considering the fact that petitioner and prosecutrix have solemnized the marriage on 23.04.2024 and are living together and enjoying happy married life, their request is considered in view of the following pronouncements of Apex Court and Coordinate Benches:-
(i) Apex Court in the matter of Ananda D.V. vs. State & Anr. Criminal Appeal Nos.394-395 of 2021 by order dated 12.04.2021 quashed the FIR in the almost similar circumstances.

entities.text: Ananda D.V. vs. State & Anr. Criminal Appeal Nos.394-395 of 2021
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant paras are as under:-
"The gravamen of the allegations in the FIR filed by the private respondent was that the appellant had promised her that he will marry her, which promise was not kept by the appellant.
The FIR was registered on 17.09.2013.
It is not in dispute that after the registration of FIR, the parties were able to resolve their differences and eventually got married on 11.10.2014.
The appellant as well as private respondent represented by Ms. Meenakshi Arora, learned senior counsel jointly state that they are enjoying happy married life.

sentences.text: A joint request is, therefore, made on behalf of the appellant and the private respondent that the FIR registered on 17.09.2013 be quashed as it was the outcome of some misunderstanding between the parties.

Considering the nature of allegations in the FIR and the realization of the fact that due to miscommunication FIR came to be registered at the relevant point of time which issues/misunderstanding have now been fully resolved and the parties are happily married since 11.10.2014, the basis of FIR does not survive.
Rather registering such FIR was an ill- advised move on the part of the private respondent, is the stand now taken before us.
It is seen that the appellant and private respondent are literate and well-informed persons and have jointly opted for quashing of the stated FIR.
Taking overall view of the matter, therefore, in the interest of justice, we accede to the joint request of quashing of FIR in the peculiar facts of the present case.
Hence, these appeals must succeed.
The impugned judgment and order is set aside.
Instead, the Writ Petition filed by the appellant for quashing is allowed, as a result of which, all steps taken on the basis of impugned FIR be treated as effaced from the record in law."

(ii) Coordinate Bench in the matter of Rahul Chaudhary vs. State of M.P. and Anr. by order dated 13.02.2023 passed in M.Cr.C. No.790/2021 after relying the judgment of Apex Court in the matter of Ananda (supra) quashed the FIR registered under Sections 376(2) (n), 506, 365 of IPC and Section 66(E) of Information Technology Act on the basis of compromise.

sentences.text: (iii) Coordinate Bench in the matter of Lalit Silkigar vs. State of M.P. and Ors. by order dated 02.09.2023 passed in M.Cr.C. No.17409/2023 quashed the FIR and criminal proceedings on the basis of the compromise registered under Sections 363, 366 and 376 of IPC read with Section 3/4 of POCSO Act and Sections 3(1)(w) and 3 (2)(va) of S.C.& S.T. (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

(v) Coordinate Bench in the matter of Ayush Tomar and Anr. vs. State of M.P. and Ors. by order dated 09.10.2023 passed in M.Cr.C. No.36139/2023 in the similar circumstances on the ground that after registration of FIR accused and prosecutrix have entered into wedlock and they are living together, quashed the FIR registered under Sections 363, 366A, 368, 376(3), 376 (2) (n) of IPC and Section 5L/6, 17 of POCSO Act.
